title: 7 Best Dual Fuel Inverter Generators (2026): Watts on Propane
description: The Champion 201319 is the best dual fuel inverter generator for most: 3,150 running watts on propane, 61 dBA and CO Shield. 7 picks compared on propane.
dek: The Champion 201319 is the best dual fuel inverter generator for most: 3,150 running watts on propane, 61 dBA and CO Shield.
intro: The best dual fuel inverter generator for most people in 2026 is the **[Champion 4500-Watt Electric Start Dual Fuel](/gear/champion-201319/)**. The dual fuel inverter to buy for most homes and RVs: enough propane watts for essentials, CO shutoff and a noise rating with a stated distance.
Seven inverter generators that also run on propane, compared on what they make on propane, how long a 20 lb tank lasts and how loud they are rated.

The Champion 201319 is the best dual fuel inverter generator for most homes: 3,150 running watts on propane, a 61 dBA rating at 23 feet and CO Shield shutoff at 99.2 lb. Your load list, and whether you need 240 volts, changes the answer. Below: 7 picks, propane derating, sizing and run time on a 20 lb tank.
quickAnswer: The Champion 4500-Watt Electric Start Dual Fuel Inverter Generator with CO Shield (201319) is our #1 pick (best overall). The dual fuel inverter to buy for most homes and RVs: enough propane watts for essentials, CO shutoff and a noise rating with a stated distance.

picks.label: Best Overall
writeup: The 201319 earns the top spot by doing everything a dual fuel inverter needs to do without a weak spot. Champion rates it at 3,500 running watts on gasoline and 3,150 on propane, with 4,500 starting watts on either fuel, which matters when a refrigerator compressor or a sump pump kicks on. The 61 dBA rating is measured at 23 feet, one of the few noise figures on this list with a stated distance. On a 20 lb cylinder Champion lists up to 21 hours at a quarter load, and 14 hours on the 2.25-gallon gasoline tank. The panel has a TT-30R for a 30-amp RV, a 5-20R household duplex and a 12V outlet, and CO Shield shuts the engine off if carbon monoxide builds up around it. Start is electric with a pull cord as backup, and the warranty is three years. The limits: it is 120V only, so it cannot feed a 240V panel or well pump, and the gas tank is small. Champion also sells the 201321 open-frame version, rated at 3,650 / 3,285 running watts, 64 dBA and 92.6 lb.

picks.label: Best Step Up
writeup: The iQ5200DF is the pick when the Champion's 3,150 propane watts feel tight. Generac rates it at 3,900 running and 5,200 starting watts on gasoline and 3,500 running and 4,700 starting on propane, from a 223cc engine with push-button electric start and a pull-cord backup. Run time is its strongest spec: Generac lists 11 hours at half load and 20 hours at a quarter load on a 20 lb cylinder, and 9 and 15 hours on the 3.2-gallon gasoline tank. COsense shuts the engine down if carbon monoxide builds up, and the panel carries two GFCI 5-20R outlets, a 120V 30-amp L5-30R locking outlet and USB-A and USB-C ports. It is parallel ready with Generac's kit #7668. Two caveats: Generac publishes no dBA figure, and its own sources list the weight as 111 lb on the product page and 107 lb on the spec sheet. One owner review on Lowe's describes a unit that would not run on propane, which Generac replaced, so run any new generator on propane once at home rather than for the first time in an outage.

picks.label: Best Remote Start
writeup: If you want to start the generator from indoors during a storm, this is the one. Westinghouse lists electric, remote and recoil start, and rates the iGen5000DF at 3,900 running and 5,000 peak watts on gasoline and 3,500 running and 4,500 peak on propane. Its 22-hour quarter-load run time on a 20 lb cylinder is the longest listed among the mid-size picks, and the 3.4-gallon gas tank is rated for 18 hours at the same load. The noise rating is 52 dBA, the lowest of the mid-size units, though Westinghouse does not say at what distance it was measured. The panel has a 5-20R duplex, a TT-30R for RVs and two USB ports, and it is parallel capable. The catch is safety: this version has no CO sensor. The iGen5000DFcv adds one but is recoil start only. Westinghouse's site now shows this model on the page that used to carry the iGen4500DF, which its older spec sheet rated at 3,700 / 3,330 running watts, so check which version a listing is selling.

picks.label: Best for Home Hookup
writeup: This is the dual fuel inverter for people who want to run house circuits rather than extension cords. Champion rates the 201417 at 9,000 running watts on gasoline and 8,100 on propane, with 11,000 starting watts on both fuels, enough to start a 240V well pump or a central air compressor that a 120V inverter cannot touch. The panel has two GFCI 5-20R duplexes, a 30-amp L14-30R and a 14-50R that Champion limits to 37.5 amps, so an electrician can connect it through an inlet box to a transfer switch or interlock. CO Shield is standard, and the 64 dBA rating is measured at 23 feet. The trade-offs are size and fuel. At 205.1 lb it lives on its wheels, and Champion lists 8 hours on a 20 lb cylinder at a quarter load, so a long outage on propane needs a 100 lb tank or a stack of cylinders. It does not support parallel operation.

sections.h: Best Dual Fuel Inverter Generator at a Glance

blocks.p: For most people, the best dual fuel inverter generator is the Champion 4500-Watt Electric Start Dual Fuel Inverter, model 201319. Champion rates it at 3,500 running watts on gasoline and 3,150 on propane, 61 dBA from 23 feet and 99.2 lb, with CO Shield automatic shutoff, a TT-30R RV outlet and parallel capability. That covers a refrigerator, freezer, furnace blower, lights and internet on propane.

If you need more propane watts in the same size, the Generac iQ5200DF and the Westinghouse iGen5000DF both rate 3,500 running watts on propane. For a 240V hookup through a transfer switch, step up to the Champion 201417 or the tri fuel Westinghouse iGen12000TFc, both rated at 8,100 running watts on propane. For camping or a small RV, the 39 lb Champion 201183 and the 49.6 lb WEN DF360iX are the light options.

This page covers only inverter generators that run on propane as well as gasoline. If you want the most watts per dollar from an open-frame unit, see our [best dual fuel generator](/best-dual-fuel-generator/) guide; for gasoline-only inverters, including Honda, see the [best inverter generator](/best-inverter-generator/) guide.
Noise figures are the makers' own. Only Champion states a measuring distance, and Generac and WEN publish no dBA figure for these models, so treat noise comparisons across brands as rough.

sections.h: How Did We Choose These Dual Fuel Inverters?

blocks.p: We started from inverter generators sold by established brands and rated by their makers on both gasoline and propane, then cut any model whose propane rating, run time or outlets we could not confirm from a manufacturer source. Where retail listings disagree, we used the manufacturer's figure.

We ranked on what matters in a long outage: propane running watts first, because propane is the fuel you will be on by day two, then run time on a 20 lb cylinder, carbon monoxide shutoff and outlets. Noise and weight came after that. Price did not set the order, and no brand paid for placement.

We did not run these generators ourselves; the ratings are the manufacturers' own. One naming quirk: Westinghouse's site now shows its iGen4500DF page as the iGen5000DF, with higher ratings, and its iGen11000TFc page as the iGen12000TFc, with the same running watts. Retailers still sell both names, so check the figures on the listing you buy from.

sections.h: How Much Power Does a Dual Fuel Inverter Lose on Propane?

blocks.p: About 10 percent. Every generator on this list loses between 10 and 10.3 percent of its running watts when it switches from gasoline to propane, a smaller and more consistent penalty than many open-frame dual fuel generators show. The Champion 201319 drops from 3,500 to 3,150 running watts, the Generac iQ5200DF and Westinghouse iGen5000DF from 3,900 to 3,500, and the two big 240V units from 9,000 to 8,100.

The loss is chemistry, not a flaw. Propane enters the engine as a vapor, displacing some of the air, and a small engine tuned for gasoline makes less power on that mixture. Surge ratings vary: Champion lists the same starting watts on both fuels, while Generac lowers the iQ5200DF's from 5,200 to 4,700.

Natural gas costs more again. The tri fuel Westinghouse iGen12000TFc is rated at 7,200 running watts on natural gas, 20 percent below gasoline, and needs a properly installed connection with adequate supply pressure, a job for a licensed plumber.

Propane pressure falls as the temperature drops, and a 20 lb tank feeding a generator at high load chills itself, so output can sag below the rating on a frigid night. The rule: build your load list against the propane running watts, then leave 10 to 20 percent of margin.

sections.h: What Will a Dual Fuel Inverter Run on Propane?

blocks.p: A 3,500-watt propane rating covers a refrigerator, a chest freezer, a furnace blower, lights, a TV and internet at the same time, as long as the motors start one at a time. It will not run central air or an electric range, and a 240V well pump needs one of the 8,100-watt units.

Those are typical figures from generator makers' wattage charts; your appliance label wins. Add up the running watts of everything you want on at once, then add the single largest starting surge. That total has to fit under the propane running rating, with margin.

blocks.h3: Matching the picks to a load

blocks.p: The Champion 201183, at 1,665 propane watts, covers a refrigerator plus lights and chargers. The WEN DF360iX, at 2,600, adds a freezer or a sump pump. The 3,150 to 3,500-watt class is where a realistic outage list fits: refrigerator, freezer, furnace blower, sump pump and electronics, staggered.

The 8,100-watt units are for 240V loads or several big motors, such as a 1/2 to 1 hp submersible well pump; our [well pump generator guide](/best-generator-for-well-pump/) explains sizing for a specific pump. Most 13,500 BTU RV rooftop units need around 3,000 watts to start without a soft starter, which the 3,150 to 3,500-watt picks cover on propane; our [RV generator guide](/best-rv-generator/) covers 30 and 50-amp rigs.

sections.h: How Long Does a 20 lb Propane Tank Last on a Dual Fuel Inverter?

blocks.p: Between about 8 and 22 hours at a quarter load for the generators here, and roughly half that at half load. Small and mid-size inverters stretch a cylinder because the engine slows down at light load; the big 240V units burn through one in a working day.

Read the load column before comparing. A quarter load on the iGen5000DF is under 900 watts on propane, roughly a refrigerator cycling plus lights and a modem; a half load on the iGen12000TFc is over 4,000 watts. The WEN's 14 hours and the Generac's 11 hours at half load are not a fair fight either, since half of the Generac's propane rating is 1,750 watts and half of the WEN's is 1,300.

A full 20 lb cylinder holds about 4.7 gallons of propane. For a multi-day outage, plan on three or four filled cylinders, or a 100 lb tank with a longer hose. Propane keeps for years and does not gum up a carburetor the way stale gasoline does, which is the main reason to buy dual fuel.
For most outages, start on the gasoline already in the tank, so it gets used before it ages, then switch to propane once the outage looks long.

sections.h: Dual Fuel Inverter or Open-Frame Dual Fuel Generator?

blocks.p: Buy a dual fuel inverter if you want quiet, clean power and long propane run times at moderate loads. Buy an open-frame dual fuel generator if you need the most watts for the money or 240V output on a budget. The two overlap only at the top of this list.

An inverter electronically rebuilds its output as a clean sine wave, which lets the engine change speed with the load. That is where the low noise ratings and long light-load run times come from. An open-frame generator spins at a fixed speed whatever the load, so it is louder and thirstier when lightly loaded.

The five smaller inverters here are 120V only: three have a TT-30R RV outlet and the Generac has an L5-30R locking outlet. They run appliances through heavy-duty extension cords. The Champion 201417 and Westinghouse iGen12000TFc are 120/240V with L14-30R and 14-50R outlets, so an electrician can connect them through an inlet box and a transfer switch or interlock. Our [generator transfer switch guide](/best-generator-transfer-switch/) covers matching the hardware.

If you are leaning toward a big unit, compare it with the open-frame options in our [best dual fuel generator](/best-dual-fuel-generator/) guide first; they offer similar propane output but are louder. The inverter earns its place near a bedroom window, a neighbor's fence or a campground. For standby, portable and battery options side by side, start with our [home generator for power outages](/best-home-generator-for-power-outages/) guide.

sections.h: Is Running Two Dual Fuel Inverters in Parallel Worth It?

blocks.p: Sometimes. Two mid-size dual fuel inverters linked with a parallel kit deliver close to double the output of one, and each can run from its own cylinder. All four brands list parallel capability on the 120V models here, each with its own kit sold separately.

The case for it: two units rated at 3,500 propane watts give about 7,000, and on a light day you run just one, which is quieter and burns less fuel. Each half weighs about 100 lb; the 240V units here weigh 191 and 205 lb.

The case against: parallel output is still 120V, so it will not run a 240V well pump or feed a 240V transfer switch, and you maintain two of everything. The Champion 201417 does not support parallel operation, and the iGen12000TFc pairs only with other 240V Westinghouse inverters.

sections.h: How Do You Run a Dual Fuel Inverter Safely?

blocks.p: Outdoors, at least 20 feet from the house, with the exhaust pointed away from doors, windows and vents. That is the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission's guidance, and it applies to propane exactly as it does to gasoline. Propane burns cleaner, but a propane-fueled engine still produces carbon monoxide, and CPSC estimates that portable generators cause nearly 80 carbon monoxide deaths a year on average.
CARBON MONOXIDE
Quiet is not the same as safe.

A quiet inverter tempts people to run it in a garage, on a porch or under a carport. Do not. CO Shield, COsense and CO Watchdog shut the engine off if carbon monoxide builds up around the generator, but they do not protect the people inside. Put battery-backed CO alarms on every level of the house and outside sleeping areas.
Six of the seven picks have automatic CO shutoff. The exception is the Westinghouse iGen5000DF; the iGen5000DFcv adds a CO sensor but drops electric and remote start for recoil only.

Use the hose and regulator that came with the generator, and check it for cracks before each season. Keep the cylinder upright, outside and away from the exhaust, close the valve when the generator is off, and never store cylinders in a basement or attached garage. If you smell gas at the connection, shut the valve and fix the fitting before restarting.
In bad weather, use a generator tent or cover made for open-air operation rather than pulling the unit under an overhang, and buy a heavy-gauge cord long enough to reach 20 feet.

mistakes: Every generator here loses about 10 percent of its running watts on propane. A load list that fits 3,900 gasoline watts can trip the breaker at 3,500 on propane, especially when a refrigerator compressor and a sump pump start together. Build the list against the propane rating and leave 10 to 20 percent of margin.
Expecting a 120V inverter to run the well pump

The Champion 201319, Generac iQ5200DF, Westinghouse iGen5000DF, Champion 201183 and WEN DF360iX are 120V only. Most submersible well pumps are 240V, and so are central air and electric dryers. For 240V circuits, buy the Champion 201417 or Westinghouse iGen12000TFc and have an electrician install an inlet and transfer switch.
Comparing run times at different loads

Makers quote propane run time at a quarter load, a half load or an unstated load, and a quarter load on a 3,500-watt inverter is under 900 watts. Check which load each figure assumes, and plan cylinders for the load you will actually run.
Buying the base model when you wanted CO shutoff

Some dual fuel inverters are sold with and without a CO sensor under nearly identical names, such as the Westinghouse iGen5000DF and iGen5000DFcv. Read the full model number. CO shutoff is cheap insurance, never a substitute for the 20-foot rule and indoor CO alarms.
Running a small cylinder flat out on a cold night

Propane pressure drops as a 20 lb cylinder gets cold, and output can sag below the rating just when you need the furnace blower most. Keep the tank out of the wind, avoid running at the top of the propane rating in freezing weather, and consider a larger cylinder for winter outages.
bottomLine: The Champion 201319 is the best dual fuel inverter generator for most people: 3,150 running watts on propane, a 61 dBA rating at 23 feet, CO Shield and a 30-amp RV outlet at 99.2 lb. Pick the Generac iQ5200DF or Westinghouse iGen5000DF for 3,500 propane watts, and the Champion 201417 or Westinghouse iGen12000TFc if you need 240V for a transfer switch. Whatever you buy, size it on the propane rating, keep enough filled cylinders for the outage you expect, and run it at least 20 feet from the house with CO alarms inside. That is what turns a quiet generator into a safe one.

faqs.q: What is the best dual fuel inverter generator?
faqs.a: For most homes and RVs, the Champion 4500-Watt Electric Start Dual Fuel Inverter (201319): 3,150 running watts on propane, 61 dBA at 23 feet, CO Shield and a TT-30R outlet at 99.2 lb. If you need 240V for a transfer switch, the Champion 201417 and the Westinghouse iGen12000TFc are both rated at 8,100 running watts on propane.

faqs.q: How much power does an inverter generator lose on propane?
faqs.a: About 10 percent of running watts for every model on this list. The Champion 201319 goes from 3,500 to 3,150 running watts, the Generac iQ5200DF and Westinghouse iGen5000DF from 3,900 to 3,500, and the 240V units from 9,000 to 8,100. Champion keeps starting watts equal on both fuels; Generac lowers them on propane too.

faqs.q: How long will a dual fuel inverter run on a 20 lb propane tank?
faqs.a: It depends on size and load. At a quarter load, Westinghouse lists 22 hours for the iGen5000DF, Champion 21 hours for the 201319 and Generac 20 hours for the iQ5200DF. The big 240V units manage 8 to 9 hours at a quarter load. At half load, Generac lists 11 hours for the iQ5200DF and Westinghouse 5 hours for the iGen12000TFc.

faqs.q: Does Honda make a dual fuel inverter generator?
faqs.a: Not as a factory model in the U.S. Honda's inverter generators, including the EU2200i and EU3200i, run on gasoline. Propane-capable Hondas for sale are aftermarket conversions or kits, which can affect warranty coverage. For factory propane with a full maker's warranty, choose a brand on this list.

faqs.q: Can a dual fuel inverter generator power a house?
faqs.a: A 120V model can power essentials through extension cords: a refrigerator, freezer, furnace blower, lights and internet fit under 3,500 propane watts if the motors start one at a time. Running household circuits through the panel needs a 120/240V unit like the Champion 201417 or Westinghouse iGen12000TFc, plus an electrician-installed inlet and transfer switch or interlock.

faqs.q: Can a dual fuel inverter run an RV air conditioner on propane?
faqs.a: Usually, in the 3,500-watt class. A 13,500 BTU rooftop unit typically needs around 3,000 watts to start without a soft starter, which the Champion 201319, Generac iQ5200DF and Westinghouse iGen5000DF cover on propane. The 2,600-watt WEN DF360iX is a soft-starter case, and the 1,665-watt Champion 201183 is for RVs with no air conditioning load.

faqs.q: Is a tri fuel inverter generator worth it?
faqs.a: Only if your house has natural gas service and you will pay a plumber to install a proper connection. The Westinghouse iGen12000TFc then runs at up to 7,200 running watts on natural gas with no refueling. Without a gas line the third fuel adds nothing; the dual fuel Champion 201417 does the same job.
